start: READY: user authorises email/password registration without invitations, separate professional approval, and immediate access to own workspace and matters.
boundary: Account creation and ordinary own-file use confer no professional approval or external-effect authority. Privileged approval is independently attributed, time bounded and checked on its protected operation.
implementation: Public email/password/confirmation signup has no invitation or client-selected profile, firm, role or approval. Email is a canonical sign-in handle, not verified mailbox ownership.

Successful signup returns its existing one-time recovery set but no session. Password sign-in then opens the server-owned personal workspace, new matters and owned matter reopening without professional approval.
ProfessionalApproval is a separate attributable, evidence-digest-bound, expiring, revocable operator record with compare-and-set history. No actual professional approval was issued in this task.

Only current emergency screen-exception creation/use consumes professional approval, in addition to existing matter/effect authority. Ordinary instructions, intake, advice, manual urgency and safety revocation remain available.

Durable bounded signup admission counts successes and failures, survives restart and fails closed on unavailable/corrupt state. Account uniqueness is enforced across workers without replacing credentials.
Authentication failures are neutral; the registered validation handler removes supplied secrets and unrecognised field names. Long email storage and display have explicit portable bounds.
The browser clears and conceals both passwords, owns pending registration until acknowledgement, and reports an unconfirmed transport result without asserting that no account exists.

The optional invited operator lane retains its original expiry, exact identity binding, one-time spend, sealed storage and race controls. Invalid invitation proof cannot fall through to public signup.
